[09:58] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): For what it's worth, Alastair, I don't think you did anything wrong. You sold me a good product that does what it says. I just bought more of it than I needed.
[10:10] Alastair McCrae (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Thanks. I appreciate that.
[10:13] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Practical things. What do you need for the exit?
[10:18] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): Our workflow definitions, if only so I know how to rebuild them in Zapier.
[10:24] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): You can export those through the API. I'll send instructions — and honestly, for eleven simple workflows, screenshots might be more useful than the JSON.
[10:36] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): Screenshots would be much more useful.
[10:39] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Then I'll get someone to produce those. It's not a thing we offer, but it's eleven workflows and it'll take an hour.
[10:48] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): That's kind.
[10:50] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): What about run history?
[10:52] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): Do I need it?
[10:54] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): You tell me. Is there any compliance reason you'd need to show what happened to a fault report from eighteen months ago?
[11:03] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): [pause] Possibly, actually. There's a Building Safety Act angle on fault response times.
[11:11] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Then take the export. It's better to have it and not need it.
[11:16] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): How do I get it?
[11:18] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Run events API. I'll send the pagination details, because two years of records will hit a limit and you'll assume it's broken.
[11:28] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): I definitely would have assumed that.
[11:31] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Everyone does. And I'll arrange a deletion confirmation for afterwards with an actual date on it.
[11:39] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): Thank you.
[11:41] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Your contract ends the eleventh of November. Do you want read-only access past that?
[11:47] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): Two weeks would help. We'll be running both in parallel through October.
[11:53] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I'll give you until the end of November. No charge.
[11:58] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): That's generous.
[12:00] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): It's not generous, it's just not petty.
[12:03] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): [laughs] Some vendors are petty.
[12:07] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Some vendors are very petty.
[12:10] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): One last question. If we did have a smaller plan — five hundred a month, five workflows, three users, no approval forms — would you buy it?
[12:22] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): [pause] With the approval forms, yes. Without them, no, because that's the bit Zapier can't do and it's the only thing I'll actually miss.
[12:34] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): So approval forms are the feature.
[12:37] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): For a company like us, the approval forms and the run history are the whole product. The rest is capability I'll never reach.
[12:47] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): That's genuinely useful and I'll pass it on.
[12:51] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): Will anything happen?
[12:53] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Probably not. But it'll be one more data point and eventually someone counts them.
[13:00] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): [laughs] That's the most realistic thing anyone's said to me all week.
[13:06] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Thank you, Hazel. Genuinely.
[13:09] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): Thanks both. Alastair — no hard feelings.
[13:14] Alastair McCrae (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): None at all. Good luck with the compliance one.
[13:18] Hazel Wren (Operations Director, Oakhill Property): [laughs] It'll never happen. Bye.

answer.summary: In both churn post-mortems, the customers said OrbitFlow should have qualified the real operating model earlier: who would actually build workflows, whether the team had capacity, and whether the product needed a dedicated role or paid help to make it work. They also said OrbitFlow should have done a real integration assessment before purchase and, when the April connector issue surfaced in Verity’s account, sent a solutions engineer to build a working custom connector instead of only pointing to docs or a template. Oakhill additionally said OrbitFlow should have offered a smaller, cheaper plan matched to their actual usage and not sold against a future roadmap that never happened.

context.text:
=== CALL-014 (call kind: churn)
CALL ID: CALL-014
DATE: 2026-09-18
VENDOR: OrbitFlow
CUSTOMER: Verity Payments
INDUSTRY: Payments
COMPANY SIZE: 800 employees
STAGE: Churn post-mortem
DURATION: 21 minutes
PARTICIPANTS:
- Maya Chen, Account Executive, OrbitFlow
- Ruth Adeyemi, Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow
- Kwame Boateng, Head of Operations, Verity Payments
- Sarah Lindqvist, Engineering Manager, Verity Payments
TRANSCRIPT
[00:00] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Kwame, Sarah — thank you for doing this. You didn't have to.
[00:05] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): We nearly didn't, if I'm honest.
[00:08] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I know. And I want to set expectations: this isn't a save attempt. You've signed with Workato, the decision's made, and I'm not going to spend twenty minutes trying to reopen it.
[00:22] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [pause] Good. That was my concern.
[00:26] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): What I want is to understand what went wrong properly, because two years is a long time to get something wrong and I'd like to not do it again.
[00:37] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): We'll be honest then.
[00:39] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Please be.
[00:41] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I'd add — I took over this account in January, so about eight months ago. Some of what went wrong predates me and some of it doesn't, and I'd rather you told me which is which.
[00:55] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Alright. Where do you want to start?
[00:59] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): With the decision. When did you actually decide?
[01:04] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Properly? June.
[01:07] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): June.
[01:09] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Though I'd say the decision became inevitable in about February and it took us until June to admit it.
[01:17] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): February.
[01:19] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): February.
[01:21] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): That's a month after I took the account.
[01:24] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): It's not about you. I want to be clear about that.
[01:29] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I'd still like to know what happened in February.
[01:33] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): February was when we tried to build the settlement reconciliation workflow and couldn't.
[01:40] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Couldn't, or found it hard?
[01:43] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Couldn't, in the sense that the effort exceeded the value by a factor I couldn't justify to my team.
[01:51] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Tell me about it specifically.
[01:54] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Our settlement provider is a mid-sized European processor. You don't have a connector for them. Nobody does, to be fair — Workato doesn't either.
[02:06] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): So what was the difference?
[02:09] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): The difference is that we ended up writing a custom integration either way, and once you've accepted you're writing custom integrations, you start asking what the platform is actually giving you.
[02:24] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And what was the answer?
[02:26] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Orchestration and run history, which are genuinely good. But not enough on their own for what we were paying.
[02:35] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): And this is where I'd push back on Sarah slightly.
[02:39] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Go on.
[02:41] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): The connector gap was real. But it wasn't why we left. It was the thing we pointed at.
[02:49] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): What was the real reason?
[02:52] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Nobody in operations ever built anything.
[02:56] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): [pause] Say more.
[02:59] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): The entire pitch — and this is the pitch I bought, so I'm implicating myself — was that my team would own their own workflows. That we'd stop queuing behind engineering. Two years in, every single production workflow was built by Sarah's team.
[03:19] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Every one.
[03:21] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [crosstalk] So we paid a premium for a business-user platform and used it as an engineering tool. And as an engineering tool it's fine but it's not worth the premium.
[03:34] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Why didn't your team build?
[03:37] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [pause] A few reasons and none of them are flattering.
[03:42] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'd rather have unflattering.
[03:45] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): The first workflow anyone builds is hard. Not conceptually hard — fiddly. You have to understand connections, you have to understand how data moves between steps, you have to understand what happens when something's null. My operations people are good at operations. They're not good at that, and expecting them to become good at it in their spare time was naive.
[04:11] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Did you have enablement?
[04:13] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): We had a two-day onboarding at the start. Eight people attended. Six of them never touched it again.
[04:22] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): And after that?
[04:24] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Nothing, until you arrived in January and offered some sessions.
[04:29] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Which you declined.
[04:31] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Which I declined, because by January I'd already half-concluded it wasn't going to work and I didn't want to spend my team's time on it.
[04:41] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): [pause] That's useful and it's painful.
[04:46] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): You asked.
[04:48] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I did ask. What would have changed it? If I'd arrived in month three rather than month twenty?
[04:56] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Honestly, I think if someone had sat with two of my people for a week in the first quarter and got them to ship something real, we'd still be a customer.
[05:08] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): I agree with that.
[05:10] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Not a training course. Sitting with them. Building the actual thing they needed.
[05:17] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): We do offer that.
[05:19] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Do you? Nobody ever offered it to me.
[05:23] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): [pause] It's a paid professional services engagement.
[05:28] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Ah.
[05:30] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Which is possibly the problem. If the thing that makes the product succeed is a paid add-on, and the customer doesn't know they need it until it's too late —
[05:41] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Then you've designed a product that fails by default for people like me.
[05:47] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's a harsher way of putting it than I would have, but I can't argue with it.
[05:53] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Can I add the engineering perspective? Because it's different.
[05:58] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Please.
[06:00] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): My team quite liked it. The run history is genuinely better than what we'd have built. The exception queues are good. When something failed at three in the morning, we could see why, and that's not nothing.
[06:16] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): So why did you support leaving?
[06:19] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Because we were maintaining custom integrations to a platform whose main selling point was that we wouldn't have to maintain custom integrations. And because the licence cost was being justified by a benefit — business-user autonomy — that wasn't materialising.
[06:39] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Say the other thing.
[06:41] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): [pause] And because two of my engineers wanted to build it in-house and I spent eighteen months arguing against them, and eventually I ran out of arguments.
[06:53] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): What was your last argument?
[06:56] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Maintenance. It's always maintenance. And it's a good argument right up until the platform also requires maintenance, at which point you're comparing two maintenance burdens and one of them costs a hundred thousand a year.
[07:13] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Is that what you're paying Workato?
[07:16] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Less. Not dramatically less.
[07:19] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): So it isn't a price decision.
[07:22] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): It's partly a price decision, because at the margin we could justify one and not the other. But no, it's not primarily price.
[07:33] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Then what tipped it to Workato specifically?
[07:37] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Two things. Their connector for our core banking platform is genuinely better than yours. That one's just true.
[07:47] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It is true. We know.
[07:49] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): And their engineering-facing story is stronger. Recipes as code, better CI story, our engineers had opinions about it and the opinions were positive.
[08:02] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): So you've bought an engineering tool.
[08:05] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): [pause] Yes. That's fair. We've bought an engineering tool and stopped pretending.
[08:12] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Which is the honest conclusion. My team is never going to build workflows. That was my ambition and it was wrong, and rather than keep paying for the ambition I've accepted the reality.
[08:26] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Can I ask — do you think that ambition was wrong in principle, or wrong for Verity?
[08:33] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [pause] For Verity. I've seen it work elsewhere. I was at a retailer before this where the operations team genuinely did build their own things.
[08:45] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): What was different?
[08:47] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): There was a person whose job it was. Not a champion, not an enthusiast — a role, with a title, whose entire job was building and maintaining automations for the business. Half a headcount, maybe.
[09:04] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): We never had that.
[09:06] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): We never had that and I never asked for it, because I thought the product removed the need for it.
[09:14] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's — I want to write that down properly, because I think it's the most important thing you've said.
[09:21] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Which part?
[09:23] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That the product doesn't remove the need for the role. It changes what the role has to be good at.
[09:31] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Yes. That's exactly it.
[09:34] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): We do say that, in fairness. It's in the operating model guidance.
[09:40] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Is it? I've never seen the operating model guidance.
[09:44] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): [pause] Then we don't say it, do we.
[09:48] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [laughs] Not effectively.
[09:51] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Let me ask about the sales process, since I ran it. What did I get wrong?
[09:58] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): You want honesty on this too?
[10:01] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Especially on this.
[10:03] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): You sold to my enthusiasm rather than to my capability. I was excited, I said my team would own it, and nobody in your organisation asked "who specifically, and what else is on their plate?"
[10:19] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's a fair criticism.
[10:22] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): It's not that you lied. You just believed me, and you shouldn't have, because I didn't know what I was agreeing to.
[10:31] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I've started asking that question, for what it's worth. Not because of you — I don't want to claim that. But it's in my discovery now. "Name the person who'll build the second workflow."
[10:45] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): That's a good question. I wouldn't have had an answer.
[10:50] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's the point of it.
[10:52] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Can I raise the support thing? Since we're doing grievances.
[10:57] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Go ahead.
[11:00] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): The support was inconsistent. Some tickets came back in an hour with someone who clearly understood the product. Others came back in a day with a link to documentation I'd already read and cited in the ticket.
[11:16] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): That's a known problem and it's a triage problem rather than a capability problem.
[11:23] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): I assumed as much. It's not why we left. But it contributed to a general feeling that we were a small account.
[11:33] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Were you treated as a small account?
[11:36] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): [pause] Probably accurately, yes.
[11:40] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): That's the answer, isn't it. You were an eighty-thousand-pound account in a book of accounts where that's below median.
[11:50] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): I'd worked that out.
[11:52] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Most customers do.
[11:55] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Is there anything we could have done in the last six months? Genuinely, not rhetorically.
[12:02] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [pause] Probably not. By March we'd started the Workato evaluation and once that starts it has its own momentum. People invest in it, they want to be right.
[12:16] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): There was a moment in April.
[12:19] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Was there?
[12:21] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): When the Workato PoC hit the same connector problem we'd hit with you. For about two weeks it looked like we'd have the same issue either way.
[12:33] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): What happened?
[12:35] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): They put a solutions architect on it for three days and built us a working custom connector as part of the evaluation. Not billed.
[12:46] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): [pause] Ah.
[12:49] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): That's when it was over, if you want the specific moment.
[12:54] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Did anyone from our side know about the connector problem in April?
[12:59] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): I mentioned it on a call. Not as an emergency. As a thing I was dealing with.
[13:06] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I remember that call.
[13:08] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): You said you'd look into whether there was a template.
[13:12] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): And I did, and there wasn't, and I emailed you saying there wasn't.
[13:18] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): You did. That was an accurate and completely useless answer.

[13:46] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): For an eighty-thousand-pound account at renewal risk? [pause] I'd have had to argue for it. I might have lost.
[13:56] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's a thing I'm going to raise internally.
[13:59] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): For what it's worth, I don't think you should have kept us. I think we were the wrong customer for the product, or the product was sold to us for the wrong reason.
[14:11] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Which of those?
[14:13] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [pause] Both, slightly.
[14:16] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Alright. Let me ask about the practical side. What do you need from us for the exit?
[14:23] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Workflow definitions and run history exported. I've already pulled the definitions through the API and they came out fine.
[14:32] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Run history?
[14:34] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): That's the one I want to check. We need eighteen months of run records for audit purposes. Not for Workato — for our own compliance.
[14:45] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Through the run events API. I'll send the pagination details because eighteen months is a lot of records and people usually hit a limit and assume it's broken.
[14:57] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): That would be useful.
[15:00] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): How long do you need access after the contract ends?
[15:04] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): When does it end?
[15:06] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Thirty-first of October.
[15:08] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): I'd want until the end of November to be safe. The export will take longer than anyone thinks.
[15:15] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I can do read-only access through November at no charge. I'd rather you had a clean exit than a scramble.
[15:24] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): You'd do that?
[15:26] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Yes, and I'd do it for two reasons. One, it's the right thing. Two, you'll be at another company in three years.
[15:36] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [laughs] That's very honest.
[15:39] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It's both true things at once.
[15:42] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): I appreciate it either way.
[15:45] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): And data deletion afterwards? You'll want that documented.
[15:50] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Yes. Our compliance team will ask for a deletion certificate.
[15:56] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I'll get that arranged and I'll tell you the timeline for it rather than saying "shortly after termination."
[16:04] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Thank you.
[16:06] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Anything else practical?
[16:09] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): There are two workflows still running that we haven't migrated. They'll be done by mid-October.
[16:16] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): What are they?
[16:18] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Merchant onboarding notifications and a daily reconciliation report.
[16:24] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Neither of which will break anything if they stop.
[16:28] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): The reconciliation one would be noticed. Not catastrophically.
[16:33] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I'll flag them so nobody deactivates anything early.
[16:38] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Can I ask one more question and then I'll let you go?
[16:42] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Go on.
[16:44] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): If you were advising another operations director who was about to buy a workflow platform — any workflow platform, not ours — what would you tell them?
[16:56] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [pause] Three things. First, name the person who'll build the fifth workflow, not the first. The first one gets built by whoever's enthusiastic. The fifth one gets built by whoever's job it is.
[17:12] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's better than my version of that question.
[17:16] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Second — do the integration assessment before you buy, not after. We spent four months discovering that our most important integration didn't exist. That's a question you can answer in a week if you insist on it during the evaluation.
[17:34] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): We should have insisted.
[17:37] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): We should have insisted and we didn't, because everyone was excited.
[17:42] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And the third?
[17:44] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Third — be honest about whether you're buying a business tool or an engineering tool, because they're priced differently and they succeed differently, and if you buy one and use the other you'll be unhappy for two years.
[18:00] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's the whole thing, isn't it.
[18:03] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): That's the whole thing.
[18:06] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Can I add one for the record?
[18:09] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Please.
[18:11] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Whatever platform you buy, get the exported definition of a real workflow during the evaluation and have an engineer read it. Not the demo. A real one, with branching. Because that tells you whether you'll be able to review changes, and it takes ten minutes, and almost nobody does it.
[18:33] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Someone did that to us last month, actually.
[18:37] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Did we pass?
[18:39] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): [laughs] I think so. It's ongoing.
[18:43] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Good.
[18:45] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Can I ask what would bring you back? In three years, at another company or here.
[18:52] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): An honest answer to "who will build the fifth workflow", and a proposal that includes whatever it costs to make that person real. If someone had said to me "this is eighty thousand for the platform and twenty-five for six months of someone sitting with your team", I might have said no. But I'd have said no with my eyes open, or said yes and it would have worked.
[19:19] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's a product and pricing point, not a sales point.
[19:24] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): It's a bit of both.
[19:26] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It's a bit of both. I'm going to take it to our product team, and I'll tell you honestly that I don't know whether anything will change.
[19:36] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): That's fine. I've been on the other side of that.
[19:41] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Right. What you'll get from us — the run events API pagination details, read-only access through November, the deletion certificate with an actual timeline, and a note flagging the two live workflows so nothing gets switched off early.
[19:59] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): That covers it.
[20:01] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And genuinely, thank you. Most people don't take this call.
[20:07] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Most people don't ask properly. You asked properly.
[20:12] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'd like to send you what I write up, if that's alright. So you can tell me if I've misrepresented anything.
[20:20] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): Send it. I'll read it.
[20:23] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): I'll read it more carefully than he will.
[20:26] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [laughs] That's true. Thanks both.
[20:30] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): Thank you. And I'm sorry about February.
[20:34] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): You weren't there in February.
[20:37] Ruth Adeyemi (Customer Success Manager, OrbitFlow): I was there in April.
[20:39] Kwame Boateng (Head of Operations, Verity Payments): [pause] Yes. Alright. Thank you, Ruth.
[20:44] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Bye both.
[20:46] Sarah Lindqvist (Engineering Manager, Verity Payments): Bye.

context.text:
=== CALL-007 (call kind: prospect)
CALL ID: CALL-007
DATE: 2026-07-16
VENDOR: OrbitFlow
PROSPECT: Greenline Energy Services
INDUSTRY: Renewable energy field services
COMPANY SIZE: 2,300 employees
STAGE: Discovery
DURATION: 27 minutes
PARTICIPANTS:
- Maya Chen, Account Executive, OrbitFlow
- Jon Bell, Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow (joined at 09:12)
- Carlos Mendes, Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services
- Lucy Hart, Field Systems Product Manager, Greenline Energy Services
TRANSCRIPT
[00:00] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Hi both. Quick heads up — Jon, our solutions engineer, is stuck on another call and will join around ten past. So it's me for the first bit, which means if you ask me something deeply technical I'll write it down rather than guess.
[00:16] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): That's fine. Can you hear me alright? I'm at a site, the line's not brilliant.
[00:22] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): You're a bit windy but you're clear.
[00:25] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): [laughs] Story of my life.
[00:28] Lucy Hart (Field Systems Product Manager, Greenline Energy Services): I'm at a desk, so if Carlos drops I can carry on.
[00:33] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Perfect. So — tell me what's actually happening today.
[00:38] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): Right. So the core of it is field exceptions. An installation gets blocked — equipment hasn't turned up, or somebody doesn't have the right permission, or access to the site isn't arranged. And the thing is, that exception is visible. It's in the system.
[00:57] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): But?
[00:59] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): But supervisors still coordinate the remediation through phone calls and spreadsheets. So we can see the problem in three different dashboards and the actual fixing of it happens over the phone.
[01:14] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): So it's not a visibility problem.
[01:17] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): It's absolutely not a visibility problem. We've got more visibility than we know what to do with. It's a — I don't know what you'd call it.
[01:27] Lucy Hart (Field Systems Product Manager, Greenline Energy Services): It's a coordination problem.
[01:29] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): It's a coordination problem, yeah. Nothing moves the work along.
[01:34] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's actually a distinction I wish more people made. We see two separate things — connecting systems, which you've largely done, and operating the process on top of the connections, which is where the pain usually sits.
[01:50] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): Then you've got us.
[01:53] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): How long does a blocked installation typically sit?
[01:57] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): Depends who's on. Some supervisors are brilliant and it's an hour. Others, it's two days.
[02:05] Lucy Hart (Field Systems Product Manager, Greenline Energy Services): That variance is the actual problem, I'd say. It's not that the average is bad. It's that we can't predict it.
[02:14] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Do you have numbers?
[02:16] Lucy Hart (Field Systems Product Manager, Greenline Energy Services): Some. We have outcome metrics — installations completed, first-time-fix rate, that sort of thing. Operational telemetry is weaker. We can tell you something was late. We're much worse at telling you why, or which dependency failed, or whether the same failure happened fifteen times last month.
[02:38] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That last one comes up in literally every one of these conversations.
[02:44] Lucy Hart (Field Systems Product Manager, Greenline Energy Services): I imagine it does.
[02:47] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Let me try a candidate workflow and you tell me if it's the right one. An installation is blocked because equipment or permissions are missing. The system creates the appropriate remediation task, notifies regional operations, and keeps Dynamics updated as the issue changes state.
[03:08] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): [pause] That's — yeah. That's it. The last part especially.
[03:14] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Why the last part?
[03:16] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): Because right now Dynamics goes stale the moment a human starts working the problem by phone. So the record says "blocked, awaiting equipment" and actually the equipment arrived yesterday and someone's already rescheduled it, but nobody's updated the system because they were busy fixing it.
[03:38] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And then your reporting is wrong.
[03:41] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): Then everything downstream is wrong. Power BI's beautiful and it's lying.
[03:47] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): [laughs] That's a good line.
[03:50] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): It's not mine, someone said it in a steering meeting and I've been stealing it ever since.
[03:57] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): One caveat I'd expect you to raise — what happens when it goes wrong? Missing data, an API timing out, an approver doing nothing for two days?
[04:08] Lucy Hart (Field Systems Product Manager, Greenline Energy Services): You're asking our question for us.
[04:11] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'd rather ask it than have it asked in month three.
[04:16] Lucy Hart (Field Systems Product Manager, Greenline Energy Services): Then yes. That's exactly what we'd want to test. The happy path is not the difficult part.
[04:23] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And there's a specific one for you that I want to raise, because I looked at your notes. Connectivity from some field locations is intermittent, so workflows can't assume the mobile app is always online.
[04:38] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): Correct. And this is the thing that kills most vendors.
[04:43] Lucy Hart (Field Systems Product Manager, Greenline Energy Services): We had one demo where the entire premise was real-time push notifications to engineers. Which is lovely until you're in a valley in mid-Wales.
[04:55] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): Or Scotland. Half our Scottish sites, you get one bar if you stand on the transformer housing.
[05:03] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Please tell me nobody stands on the transformer housing.
[05:07] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): [laughs] I'm not answering that.
[05:11] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Right, I'm writing that down as a question for Jon rather than answering it myself. My general understanding is you'd design the workflow so the sync from the mobile app is eventual rather than assumed, and the workflow tolerates delay rather than treating it as failure. But how that's actually built is his answer, not mine.
[05:33] Lucy Hart (Field Systems Product Manager, Greenline Energy Services): That's the right shape of answer at least.
[05:37] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Talk me through the stack.
[05:39] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): Microsoft Dynamics 365. Power BI. Teams. Azure Functions. And a custom field-service mobile app that we built ourselves.
[05:51] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): The mobile app — does it expose APIs?
[05:55] Lucy Hart (Field Systems Product Manager, Greenline Energy Services): It does. That's my area. It's got a reasonable API surface, it's documented, it's not beautiful but it works.
[06:04] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And which of these is the system of record?
[06:08] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): Dynamics for the work order. The mobile app for what actually happened on site. And those two disagree more often than I'd like.
[06:19] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And Power BI?
[06:21] Lucy Hart (Field Systems Product Manager, Greenline Energy Services): Power BI is an output layer. It's not a system of record, it just reads.
[06:27] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Understood. And I'm guessing you have Power Automate.
[06:32] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): [laughs] Of course we have Power Automate.
[06:36] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Tell me honestly how it's going.
[06:39] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): We use it heavily. And we get favourable licensing on it, which matters more than I'd like it to.
[06:47] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): But.
[06:49] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): But complex flows are hard for operations to troubleshoot. When something breaks, it comes to my team, and my team is six people supporting two and a half thousand.
[07:02] Lucy Hart (Field Systems Product Manager, Greenline Energy Services): And there's a knowledge problem. The people who can debug it aren't the people who understand the process.
[07:10] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): So I'm exploring alternatives. That's what this is. I want to be honest that it's exploration, not a procurement process.
[07:20] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I appreciate that and I'd rather know now.
[07:24] Lucy Hart (Field Systems Product Manager, Greenline Energy Services): I should clarify something Carlos said, actually. About regional ownership.
[07:30] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): Go on.
[07:32] Lucy Hart (Field Systems Product Manager, Greenline Energy Services): Carlos tends to say most regions can't maintain their own automations, and that's broadly true. But two of them already have local Power Automate specialists. So the operating model isn't completely centralised today, and if we designed as though it were, those two regions would just — carry on doing their own thing.
[07:56] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): That's fair. That's a fair correction.
[08:00] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Which two regions?
[08:02] Lucy Hart (Field Systems Product Manager, Greenline Energy Services): North and — Carlos, is it South West or South Central?
[08:07] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): South West. [inaudible] — sorry, say again?
[08:12] Lucy Hart (Field Systems Product Manager, Greenline Energy Services): North and South West.
[08:15] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's actually useful. Those two could be your pilot builders rather than your resistance.
[08:22] Lucy Hart (Field Systems Product Manager, Greenline Energy Services): [pause] That's a thought.
[08:25] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): That's a better thought than I'd had, honestly.
[08:29] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It's not mine originally. Most of the successful rollouts I've seen started with the people who were already building things, not the people who needed convincing.
[08:41] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): Hm. Lucy, note that down.
[08:44] Lucy Hart (Field Systems Product Manager, Greenline Energy Services): Noted.
[08:47] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): While we're waiting for Jon — can I ask a slightly personal question?
[08:52] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): Go on.
[08:54] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Were you field originally? You talk about it like someone who's been out there.
[09:00] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): Six years. Wind, mostly. I was a technician then a supervisor and then somebody made the mistake of putting me near a computer.
[09:10] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): [laughs] That explains a lot.
[09:12] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): — hello? Sorry. Sorry, I'm here. Apologies, that ran over.
[09:18] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): No problem. Jon, quick catch-up. Greenline are Dynamics, Power BI, Teams, Azure Functions, and a custom field-service mobile app they built themselves which exposes APIs. Power Automate incumbent, used heavily, favourable licensing. The use case is blocked installations — create remediation task, notify regional ops, keep Dynamics current as the issue changes.
[09:44] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Got it.
[09:46] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And the one I flagged for you: connectivity from some field locations is intermittent, so workflows can't assume the mobile app is online.
[09:56] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Right. That's a real design constraint and it's a good one to raise early. Can I ask a question back?
[10:04] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): Please.
[10:06] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): When a device comes back online and syncs, do you get an event, or does the record just quietly change?
[10:14] Lucy Hart (Field Systems Product Manager, Greenline Energy Services): You get an event. The app publishes on sync.
[10:19] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Then you're in a much better position than most. The pattern would be that the workflow doesn't poll the device and doesn't assume presence. It reacts to the sync event when it arrives, and separately it has a timeout rule — if we haven't heard anything in N hours, that itself becomes an exception rather than a silent hang.
[10:42] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): So the not-hearing is also an event.
[10:46] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): The absence of a signal is a signal. Yes. And that's usually the bit people forget to build.
[10:53] Lucy Hart (Field Systems Product Manager, Greenline Energy Services): We definitely haven't built that.
[10:56] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Almost nobody has, first time round.
[11:00] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): What happens to the run in the meantime? Does it just sit there?
[11:05] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Each run keeps state, so yes, it can sit in a waiting state without consuming anything or falling over. You can branch on data, pause for approvals, retry external actions, set timeout rules, and send an exception into a queue rather than failing silently.
[11:24] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): Can the queue be owned by a team? Because our supervisors rotate and if it's assigned to a person, that person's on leave.
[11:34] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Yes. Route to a group, resolve a person dynamically from a field, or use an on-call style fallback. And the run history persists so you can see the inputs, which steps ran, and where it stopped.
[11:50] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): On-call is interesting for us. Field ops genuinely does run a rota.
[11:57] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Then that maps well. I'd want to look at how the rota is stored, because ideally we resolve from your source of truth rather than maintaining a second copy.
[12:09] Lucy Hart (Field Systems Product Manager, Greenline Energy Services): It's in Dynamics. Sort of.
[12:12] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): "Sort of" is doing some work in that sentence.
[12:16] Lucy Hart (Field Systems Product Manager, Greenline Energy Services): [laughs] It's in Dynamics for some regions and in a shared calendar for others.
[12:22] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Right. So that's a thing to fix before or during, not after.
[12:28] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): Add it to the list.
[12:31] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Jon, the big one. Dynamics.
[12:34] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Yeah. So let me be straight about this because it's the thing that'll decide the evaluation. Dynamics 365 and Teams you've said are mandatory. There are integration routes to Dynamics — API-based, plus our generic REST action and webhooks. What I'm not going to tell you is that we have the deepest first-class Dynamics connector on the market, because Microsoft's own tooling will always be closer to Dynamics than we are.
[13:04] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): [pause] Right.
[13:07] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): I'd rather say that now than have you find it in week four.
[13:12] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): No, I — I appreciate it. But you understand that's the whole problem.
[13:18] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): I do.
[13:20] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): The first-class Dynamics gap is the biggest issue for us. Power Automate is already embedded here. It's licensed, it's approved, the platform team likes it. For us to work around all of that, OrbitFlow has to be materially better, not marginally better.
[13:41] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's the honest framing and I'm not going to argue with it. Can I ask what "materially better" would look like?
[13:50] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): [pause] Good question.
[13:53] Lucy Hart (Field Systems Product Manager, Greenline Energy Services): Troubleshooting. If a regional supervisor can look at a failed thing and understand what happened without raising a ticket to Carlos's team, that's material.
[14:06] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): Yeah. That. And reusability — if we build the remediation pattern once and use it in eight regions, rather than eight regions each building their own.
[14:19] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Both of those are things I'd want to be tested on rather than claim. The reusability one specifically — we push people hard towards small reusable subflows rather than one big canvas, and that's the mechanism. But you should make me prove it.
[14:38] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): How would we prove it?
[14:41] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): Build the remediation flow for one region, then have someone from a different region adapt it for theirs, and time it. And have someone who didn't build it debug a deliberately broken run.
[14:56] Lucy Hart (Field Systems Product Manager, Greenline Energy Services): That's a good test.
[14:59] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): That's a very good test, actually.
[15:02] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Can I add a slightly awkward version of it? Do the same test in Power Automate at the same time. If it's not better, you should know.
[15:13] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): You're suggesting we benchmark you against the incumbent.
[15:18] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'd rather lose in week two than lose in month eight.
[15:23] Carlos Mendes (Head of Digital Operations, Greenline Energy Services): [laughs] Alright.
[15:26] Lucy Hart (Field Systems Product Manager, Greenline Energy Services): I'd have suggested it anyway.
[15:29] Maya Chen (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I know. I'd just rather say it first.
[15:33] Jon Bell (Solutions Engineer, OrbitFlow): One more integration question. The custom mobile app — you said it exposes APIs. Are those APIs reachable from outside your network?
[15:44] Lucy Hart (Field Systems Product Manager, Greenline Energy Services): They're behind Azure API Management. So yes, with authentication.

[00:09] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): [pause] OrbitFlow. That's funny.
[00:13] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Is it?
[00:15] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): We're three weeks into evaluating Tray.io. Your name came up on a list and got crossed off.
[00:23] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Crossed off by whom?
[00:25] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Me. About a month ago.
[00:28] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Can I ask why? Genuinely — I'm not going to argue, I just want to know.
[00:34] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Your website. It's very enterprise. Governance, compliance, workspace separation. We're a hundred and fifty people building robots. I looked at it and thought, that's not for us.
[00:49] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): [pause] That's a fair read of our website.
[00:53] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): You're agreeing?
[00:55] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Our marketing is aimed at companies with a governance function. You don't have one, so it isn't aimed at you.
[01:04] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): So why are you calling?
[01:06] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Because our marketing being aimed at somebody else doesn't mean the product is wrong for you. But I'd want to establish that in about four minutes rather than argue with your conclusion.
[01:19] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Go on then. Four minutes.
[01:22] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): What are you trying to do with Tray?
[01:25] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Order-to-deployment. A customer orders a robot cell, and then there's engineering config, procurement of the long-lead parts, build scheduling, factory acceptance testing, shipping, and site commissioning. Seven stages, five systems, and about four months elapsed.
[01:47] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And what goes wrong?
[01:49] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Nothing goes wrong exactly. Things just take longer than they should because stage four doesn't know stage three finished until someone mentions it in a meeting.
[02:01] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): How much of the four months is waiting?
[02:04] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): [pause] I don't know. That's part of why we're doing this.
[02:10] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Okay. How's the Tray evaluation going?
[02:14] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Well. Genuinely well. Their team's been good.
[02:19] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Then I'd say two things. First, I'm not going to tell you Tray is bad. It isn't. We lose to them and we beat them and it usually comes down to fit rather than quality.
[02:32] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): What's the second?
[02:34] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Three weeks in, with a decision coming, I'd be the third horse in a two-horse race, and that's usually a waste of everyone's time.
[02:44] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): You're talking yourself out of it again.
[02:47] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'm being realistic about it. Unless there's something in your evaluation that isn't going well, in which case I'd want to know what.
[02:57] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): [pause] There is one thing.
[03:00] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Go on.
[03:02] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Our ERP. It's a mid-market system, quite niche in manufacturing. Tray don't have a connector and we're looking at building against its API, which our one back-end developer estimates at three weeks.
[03:19] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Do you believe the estimate?
[03:21] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): [laughs] No.
[03:23] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Nobody ever does.
[03:25] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): It'll be six.
[03:27] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'd want to be honest — there's a good chance we don't have a connector either. What's the system?
[03:34] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): I'd rather not say on a cold call, if that's alright.
[03:39] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Completely fine. Then let me answer it generally. If it's a mid-market manufacturing ERP, we probably don't have a native connector, and you'd be building against the API with our generic REST action. Which is the same three weeks. Or six.
[03:57] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): So no advantage.
[04:00] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): No advantage on that specific point, no. There might be one on what happens afterwards — who maintains it, whether it's reusable across the seven stages — but that's a subtler argument and I'm not going to pretend it's decisive.
[04:17] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): You keep doing this.
[04:19] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Doing what?
[04:21] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Conceding things.
[04:23] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'd rather concede the things that are true and be believed on the things that aren't.
[04:29] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): [pause] Alright. What's the argument you would make?
[04:35] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Honestly, only one, and it's small. You said your one back-end developer would build the ERP integration. What happens when he's busy and someone in operations wants to change which stage triggers a notification?
[04:52] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): It waits.
[04:54] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): For how long?
[04:56] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): [pause] Depends. Weeks.
[04:59] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Then the question for your evaluation — for either vendor — is whether the people who own the process can change the process without him. That's testable in a week and most evaluations don't test it.
[05:15] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): How would you test it?
[05:17] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Have someone in operations, not your developer, build one real workflow. Not with the developer sitting next to them. And see what happens.
[05:29] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): [pause] That's a good test.
[05:33] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It's the test that predicts whether you're happy in two years. Run it against Tray — I mean that, run it against Tray, you're three weeks in and it costs you nothing.
[05:46] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): And if they pass?
[05:48] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Then buy Tray. You'll have made a good decision for a good reason.
[05:54] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): [laughs] You are the strangest salesperson I've spoken to this year.
[05:59] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'll take that.
[06:01] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Look — I'm not going to restart the evaluation. We've got a decision date and I'm not moving it.
[06:09] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I wouldn't ask you to.
[06:11] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): But I'll do this. Send me something short — not a deck — on how you'd approach the seven-stage thing, and specifically on the operations-can-change-it question. If we go with Tray and it doesn't work out, I'll know who to call.
[06:29] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'd rather have that than a demo you sit through politely.
[06:34] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): When's the decision?
[06:36] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Mid-October. Fourteenth, I think, or thereabouts.
[06:42] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Would it be worth a thirty-minute call before mid-October? Not a pitch. I'd walk through how I'd structure the seven stages and you can use the thinking whichever vendor you pick.
[06:56] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): You'd do that knowing we'll probably go with Tray?
[07:01] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): You're a hundred and fifty people building robots. You'll be four hundred people in three years and you'll be buying something else. I'd rather be the person who was useful.
[07:14] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): [pause] That's a long game.
[07:17] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It's the only game in a market this small.
[07:21] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Alright. Send the note. If it's good I'll do the thirty minutes.
[07:27] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Can I ask one thing before you go?
[07:30] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Go on.
[07:32] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): The four months. Have you got a number for what a month costs you?
[07:37] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): A month of delay on a cell? Roughly, we recognise revenue on commissioning, so — a month is a month of revenue on a two hundred thousand pound order.
[07:50] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And how many orders in flight?
[07:53] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Eleven at the moment.
[07:55] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Then if instrumenting the seven stages tells you where two weeks are going, that's a much bigger number than either vendor's licence.
[08:05] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): [pause] That's the slide I need for my board, isn't it.
[08:10] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It's the slide you need regardless of who you buy from.
[08:14] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): [laughs] Send the note, Leo.
[08:17] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I will. Thanks Rafael.
[08:20] Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics): Bye.

context.text:
=== CALL-003 (call kind: prospect)
CALL ID: CALL-003
DATE: 2026-06-11
VENDOR: OrbitFlow
PROSPECT: Cedar & Finch
INDUSTRY: E-commerce
COMPANY SIZE: 180 employees
STAGE: Discovery / demo
DURATION: 17 minutes
PARTICIPANTS:
- Leo Grant, Account Executive, OrbitFlow
- Sophie Reed, Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch
- Marcus Lee, Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch
TRANSCRIPT
[00:00] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Hi both. Sophie, Marcus — thanks for making time.
[00:04] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Hi. Marcus is on his phone, he's between things.
[00:09] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): Yeah, sorry, I'm walking. I'll be at a desk in five.
[00:14] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): No problem. So normally I'd spend twenty minutes on discovery before showing anything, but —
[00:21] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Can we not?
[00:22] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): [laughs] Go on.
[00:25] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): We've done three of these in a fortnight. I can recite our own pain points. Can we just see it and I'll interrupt when something matters?
[00:35] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Deal. I'll ask about four questions along the way rather than up front. Fair?
[00:41] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Fair.
[00:43] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): One thing before I share — I'm on my own today. Nina, our solutions engineer, is with another customer. So if you ask me something properly technical I'm going to say "I'll come back to you" rather than make it up.
[00:58] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): I'd prefer that, honestly.
[01:02] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Right. Sharing. [pause] Can you see it?
[01:07] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Yep.
[01:09] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): So this is the workflow builder. Triggers and actions on the left, the flow in the middle, and whatever step you've clicked gets its config on the right.
[01:20] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I've pre-built something that I think is roughly your world. High-value order comes in, there's a fulfilment exception on it, we open a ticket, we ping a channel, we update a tracker.
[01:34] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): That's — yeah, that's almost exactly it. Detect high-value orders with fulfilment exceptions, Zendesk ticket, right Slack channel, and update our Airtable exception tracker.
[01:48] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Then let me just run it. [pause] So it's triggered off the order event, it checks the value threshold, it checks the exception flag, and then it branches.
[02:01] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Stop there. What happens if the order data's incomplete?
[02:07] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Good. So — this branch here. If the required fields aren't populated it doesn't just carry on, it drops into an exception queue.
[02:17] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Owned by who?
[02:19] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): A team, not a person. You can route to a group, or resolve a person dynamically off a field, or use an on-call style fallback.
[02:29] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Okay. That's relevant, because — Marcus, are you back?
[02:34] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): I'm here, I'm sitting down.
[02:37] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Tell him the number.
[02:39] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): Right, so. We've got more than sixty Zapier automations. Six-zero. And several of them are owned by people who don't work here any more.
[02:50] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): How do you find out when one breaks?
[02:53] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): When a customer complains.
[02:56] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): [pause] Right.
[02:59] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): That's not a joke, that's genuinely the detection mechanism.
[03:04] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): It's the honest answer.
[03:07] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It's a very common answer. It's just usually not said out loud in the first ten minutes.
[03:14] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): Well, we're not going to fix it by pretending.
[03:18] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): No. Okay, so let me show you the bit that speaks to that. [pause] This is run history. Filter by workflow, status, time. Open any run and you see every step, the inputs, the outputs, timings, retries.
[03:36] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Can I set an alert on a failure rate rather than an individual failure? Because sixty automations, if I get an email per failure I'll just filter them into a folder and never look at it.
[03:50] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Yes — you can alert when error rates cross a threshold. And that's the right instinct, everyone who alerts per-failure ends up ignoring all of them.
[04:01] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Learned that one the hard way.
[04:05] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): Can I correct something Sophie said in the email, actually?
[04:09] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Go on.
[04:11] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): I think I may have overstated the Zendesk angle earlier. Support feels like the loudest problem because failures surface there — that's where the customer shouts. But honestly, probably only about a quarter of the automations actually touch Zendesk.
[04:31] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's a really useful correction. What do the other three quarters touch?
[04:37] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): Shopify mostly. Klaviyo. Some Airtable stuff.
[04:42] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Let me give you the full list. Shopify, Zendesk, Klaviyo, Slack, Airtable, and Zapier holding it all together with string.
[04:53] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And of those, which one is the one that has to work perfectly?
[04:58] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Shopify. A native Shopify trigger is — that's important. If that's a polling hack I'm not interested.
[05:07] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Understood. I'm going to be careful here — I believe the Shopify integration is native and event-driven, but I'm not going to swear to the exact trigger coverage without checking. That's a Nina question and I'll get you a written answer.
[05:24] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Fine.
[05:26] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): What about volume? Roughly.
[05:29] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Off peak, about eight thousand orders a week. Peak is — Marcus?
[05:35] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): Peak is silly. Three, four times that in the run-up to Christmas.
[05:41] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And you're UK and EU?
[05:43] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): UK and EU, yes. Which is a security question, so let me do that bit now while I remember.
[05:51] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Go for it.
[05:53] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): We need a standard DPA. SSO would be nice rather than mandatory — we're a hundred and eighty people, I'm not going to pretend we've got a zero-trust programme. And because we sell into the UK and EU I want to understand where customer data actually gets processed.
[06:14] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That last one I can answer partly. EU data residency is available on Enterprise. On Growth, I'd need to confirm the default processing region for you in writing rather than guess.
[06:28] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Enterprise. That's the expensive one.
[06:31] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's the expensive one, yes.
[06:34] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Then let's do money now, because I don't want to spend twenty minutes falling in love with this.
[06:41] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Sensible. Growth starts at eighteen hundred a month, up to thirty users, on an annual agreement.
[06:49] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): [pause] Right.
[06:52] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Say it.
[06:54] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Eighteen hundred a month is hard for a team our size. I had something closer to eight hundred, maybe a thousand, in my head.
[07:04] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's a real gap. I'm not going to pretend it isn't.
[07:09] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): I could potentially do an annual prepay if that materially changes the number. Does it?
[07:16] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): It can. I'd be lying if I said it halves it. It's a meaningful discount, not a transformation.
[07:24] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Mm.
[07:26] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): What's the Zapier bill at the moment, Soph?
[07:30] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Ours? About two hundred and something. But that's not the comparison and you know it, because the two hundred doesn't include the four hours a week you spend chasing broken ones.
[07:43] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): It's more than four.
[07:45] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): [crosstalk] I know it's more than four. I'm being generous to my own argument.
[07:50] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That is actually the argument, though. Can I ask — if you priced Marcus's time and the customer complaints, what does the current setup cost you?
[08:01] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): I genuinely don't know. Nobody's ever asked me to count it.
[08:07] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): And that's the problem with building the business case. I can't put "vibes" in a spreadsheet for the finance director.
[08:15] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): No. But you could count it for four weeks before you decide anything. That's free and it'd make the conversation much easier either way.
[08:26] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): That's — yeah. That's a fair suggestion.
[08:31] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): I can log it. It'll be depressing but I can log it.
[08:36] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Let me show you two more things and then I'll stop. [pause] This is the templates and reusable components bit. Rather than sixty separate automations, you'd typically build a handful of subflows — order lookup, notification, ticket creation — and assemble from those.
[08:57] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): So when something changes I change it in one place.
[09:02] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): In one place, yes. And that's genuinely the thing I'd point at for your sixty-Zap problem. It's not that we do things Zapier can't. It's that sixty independent Zaps is sixty things to maintain and this is more like eight.
[09:20] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Okay. That is the most compelling thing you've said.
[09:25] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): I'll take it.
[09:27] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): What about visibility of who owns what? Because the dead-employee problem is real.
[09:34] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Version history and change metadata on every workflow. So you can see what changed and when. And you'd typically define who can publish to production versus who can build in a dev workspace.
[09:49] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): We don't have a dev workspace. We don't have a dev anything.
[09:54] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): [laughs] You'd get one. That's not extra cost, it's just how it's structured.
[10:00] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Do you do the AI stuff? Everyone does the AI stuff now.
[10:05] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): We do, but I'd underplay it for you. It's optional steps inside a workflow — classification, summarisation, extracting fields out of text, drafting something a human then approves. It's not an autonomous agent thing.
[10:22] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Is there something there for us or are you being polite?
[10:27] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): There might be one. You mentioned wanting a weekly digest of recurring support reasons pushed to the e-commerce and product teams?
[10:37] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): That was me. I want that. I've wanted that for two years.
[10:42] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): That's a reasonable fit — summarise the week's tickets by theme, with links back to the underlying tickets so someone can check it.
[10:52] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): With links. Because I don't trust a summary I can't verify.
[10:57] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): You shouldn't. And that's how we'd build it — the source references stored next to the generated output.
[11:05] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Does that cost extra?
[11:07] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Usage is scoped on workflow runs and premium connectors. I'd want to model that for your volumes rather than say "no" and surprise you later.
[11:19] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Everyone says that and then there's a surprise later.
[11:23] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Then let me put the assumptions in writing and you can hold me to them.
[11:29] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Okay.
[11:32] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Can I ask about decision-making? If you did want to do this, what's the path?
[11:38] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): I can choose tools under fifteen thousand a year on my own. Above that it goes to the COO and the finance director.
[11:47] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And eighteen hundred a month is —
[11:50] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Twenty-one, six. So it goes upstairs. Which is a different conversation and a slower one.
[11:58] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Understood. That's useful to know now rather than in six weeks.
[12:04] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): I'm telling you because I'd rather not waste either of our time.
[12:09] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Appreciated. Timing?
[12:12] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): I'd like to clean up the automations before the holiday peak. Ideally something in place by early October, because after that nobody's changing anything until January.
[12:25] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): Nobody touches anything in November. Company rule.
[12:29] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Sensible rule. So realistically a decision in — August?
[12:35] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): August, if we do it.
[12:38] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): Right. Let me ask the uncomfortable one. What's the alternative? Not "do nothing" — the real alternative.
[12:47] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Honestly? Zapier and Make. I like Zapier for the simple stuff, it does what it says. And I've tested Make for the more complicated branching, which it handles better than I expected.
[13:03] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): And the concern with those?
[13:06] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Maintenance and visibility. The same two things. Make would give me the branching but I'd still have the ownership problem.
[13:16] Marcus Lee (Customer Support Manager, Cedar & Finch): And nobody here knows Make except Sophie.
[13:20] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): Which is its own ownership problem.
[13:24] Leo Grant (Account Executive, OrbitFlow): So the honest framing is: we'd have to beat Zapier plus better documentation and ownership discipline. Not beat doing nothing.
[13:35] Sophie Reed (Director of E-commerce Operations, Cedar & Finch): That's exactly right. And to be blunt — budget is the biggest risk here.
